entities.label: PETITIONER

sentences.text: This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation of Rs.6 crores for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

2. The facts leading to the filing of top noted petition are that on 19-2-2020 at about 6.30 a.m. when the petitioner Salman Shariff was riding the motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA- 05-JT-9632 from Mico bande signal towards Dairy circle on Bannerghatta road, opposite to Masjidhi Khudadadh, at that time, driver of Eicher milk lorry bearing No.KA-02-AC-3903 came in a rash and negligent manner from dairy circle towards Mico bande junction by violating traffic rules and lost control over his vehicle and ran over the centre median of the road and came to other side of the road and dashed the petitioner's motor cycle and petitioner sustained grievous injuries and shifted to Sagar hospital,
Tilaknagar, Bangalore and for better treatment again shifted to Narayana Multi speciality hospital,
Mysore and admitted as inpatient for 40 days on 2 occasions.
It is further stated that petitioner underwent surgery and discharged from the hospital and also took conservative treatment.
It is further stated that petitioner is suffering from disability and discomforts.

It is further stated that petitioner is aged 30 years, working as Senior Technical support engineer in VM Ware software India Pvt., Ltd., and drawing salary of Rs.1,55,000/-p.m. and due to accidental injuries, he is suffering from permanent disability.

entities.text: VM Ware software India Pvt., Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Hence prays to award compensation of Rs.6 crores from the respondents.
3. Inspite of due service of notice to the respondents, respondent No.1 remained absent and placed exparte.
The respondent No.2 appeared through its counsel and filed written statement.

4. The respondent No.2 in its written statement stated that it has issued insurance policy in favour of the 1 st respondent with respect to his vehicle No.KA-02-AC-3903 covering the risk of the said vehicle.
Further respondent No.2 contended all the petition averments as false.
Further contented that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is very exorbitant.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in an accident that was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Eicher milk lorry bearing reg.No.KA-02-AC-3903 on 19-2-2020 at about 6.30 a.m. at Opp.Masjidhi Khudadadh, Chandrappa nagar, Bannerghatta road, Bangalore?
Salman Shariff vs Suresh G.C on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133023177/
2 3.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?

If so, at what rate? from whom ?
4.
What order
or award ?
6. One Praveen C.-Senior Manager at Sagar hospital, Bangalore examined himself as PW.1 and got examined five witnesses as PW-2 to PW-6 and got marked Ex's.P1 to 64.
The respondent No.2 got examined one Ashwathaiah-driver as RW-1, one V.T.Vijaykumar-Retired PSI as RW-2 but no documents marked.
7. Arguments were addressed on both side.
8. Perused the entire materials placed on record.

My answers to the above issues are as follows :-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order  for the following :
 REASONS 9. ISSUE NO.1 : In order to prove that the accident had occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Eicher milk lorry bearing reg.No.KA-02-AC- 2903, father and next friend of the petitioner Maqbool Shariff got examined himself as PW.4 and got marked 21 documents as Ex-P17 to 38 i.e.,FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, charge sheet, IMV report, rough sketch, wound certificate, discharge summaries, adhaar card, pan card, marks card, adhaar card,
pan card, authorisation letter, medical bills, receipts, 65B Evidence Act.

10. The evidence on record reveals that on the basis of the complaint lodged by Naiman Shariff S/o Makhbhul Shariff Adugodi traffic police registered FIR as per Ex-P17 and conducted thorough and detailed investigation and filed charge sheet as per Ex-P20 against the driver of the milk truck for offences punishable u/sec 279, 338 of IPC by holding that on 19-2-2020 at about 6.30 to 7.00 a.m.
accused drove the Eicher milk truck bearing No.KA-02-AC- 3903 on the Bannerughatta road from dairy circle towards Micco signal in a rash and negligent manner and ran over the half feet mediator situated in the middle of the road and drove in the wrong side and hit to the motor cycle driven by the petitioner who was coming from the Mico Bande signal towards dairy circle and thereby caused the accident.

It was held that the accident had been caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Eicher milk truck vehicle No.KA-02-AC-3903.
11.
Apart from this, though PW-4 was cross-examined at length, but nothing worth was elicited from his mouth.
Moreover PW-4 is not an eye witness.

On the other hand, respondent seriously disputed the cause and manner and occurrence of the accident and contended that the accident had been taken place due to the sole rash and negligent driving of the petitioner himself.

The counsel for the respondent No.2 got examined driving of the Eicher Milk Truck vehicle No.KA-02-AC-3903 as Salman Shariff vs Suresh G.C on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133023177/
3 RW-1 wherein RW-1 deposed that on the date of accident, he was driving the Eicher milk truck from Mico layout dairy towards Bannerughatta main road, at that time, in front of the dairy, petitioner came by driving the motor cycle from the back side of the Eicher lorry and hit to the back portion of the lorry and thereby caused the accident.

entities.text: Salman Shariff vs Suresh G.C on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further RW-1 contended that the sketch Ex-P23 produced by the I.O. is wrong.
12. But however RW-1 himself in his cross-examination
clearly admitted that on 19-02-2020 he was driving the vehicle at 6.30 a.m. and it was two way direction road width of 30 feet each.
Further RW-1 admitted that there was a divider of 1 feet in the middle of the road.
Even RW-1 admitted that the accident had been taken place in front of the mosque.
On perusal of Ex-P19 spot mahazar, it clearly shows that the accident had been taken place in front of the Kudhad mazid.
Even as per Ex-P23 sketch, spot of accident is in front of the Kudhad maszid.

Though RW-1 denied the suggestion that on that day when he was coming from dairy circle towards Micco layout, at that time, the petitioner was coming in his motor cycle from Micco layout towards dairy circle and at that time, RW-1 drove his vehicle in a speed manner and drive over the divider and hit to the two wheeler of the petitioner which was coming from the opposite direction on the other side of the road and thereby caused the accident.
But RW-1 admitted that the police have filed the charge sheet against him and even all the police documents depicts the same.
13. Further though RW-1 contended that all the police documents are wrong and the accident had not been taken place a per the police documents.
But RW-1 has not filed any complaint against the rider of the motor cycle nor taken any legal action.
Even RW-1 has not challenged the charge sheet filed against him and has admitted the said fact.
Further even RW-1 has not denied the fact that in the criminal case, he has pleaded the guilty and paid the fine.
RW-1 only contended that the owner of the vehicle has paid the fine amount and the said case has been closed.

If at all as per the version of the RW-1, if the accident had not been taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of petitioner vehicle, certainly, RW-1 would have filed the complaint or challenged the charge sheet or have contested the case.
But RW-1 has not taken any such action.
Under such facts and circumstances the contention of the RW-1 cannot be believed.
14. Apart from this, though RW-1 contended that when he was moving on the left side of the milk dairy, at that time, petitioner has came and hit to his vehicle from the hind portion.
But on perusal of the MV report Ex-P22 of the Eicher vehicle, it clearly shows that there was front right side bumper damaged and no damages has been caused to the back side portion of the vehicle.
Even Ex-P21 clearly shows that the accident had been taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the RW-1.

Even counsel for the respondent No.2 got examined the I.O. by name V.T.Vijayakumar who deposed to have conducted the investigation in Crime No.24/2020 and during investigation he found that Ashwathaiah was driving the Eicher milk truck and came in the Bannerughatta road from dairy circle towards Mico bande and drove over the mediator situated in the middle of the road and came to the wrong side of the road and hit to the motor cycle driven by the petitioner who was coming from Micco bande towards dairy road in the opposite direction.
Further RW-2 clearly stated that he has prepared the spot sketch.

Further though counsel for the respondent No.2 himself cross examined RW-2 by treating him as a hostile, but even in the cross-examination also nothing was elicited from the mouth of the RW-2 in favour of the respondents.

On the other hand, RW-2 clearly Salman Shariff vs Suresh G.C on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133023177/
4 stated that accident has been caused as the driver of the lorry drove the lorry over the divider and came to the wrong side and hit to the motor cycle and caused the accident.

entities.text: Salman Shariff vs Suresh G.C on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further RW-2 clearly stated that the divider is of  feet and as a driver of the lorry was driving the lorry in speed manner and ran over the divider and caused accident.

It is pertinent to note here that this fact is not denied by the counsel for the respondent No.2 at least by putting single suggestion and denied all the suggestions made by the counsel for the respondent No.2.

Further counsel for the respondent No.2 himself by putting the suggestion that generally accused will plead guilty in all such cases and in the present case the owner of the lorry has paid the fine amount for which RW-2 pleaded his ignorance.

Even in the cross-examination made by the petitioner, counsel for the RW-2 clearly stated that the front portion of the lorry has been damaged and apart from this, respondent counsel has not at all examined any of the eye witness to disprove the case of the petitioner and the police documents except the self serving statement of RW-1 driver there is no other corroborative evidence in support of same.
Hence evidence of RW-1 driver cannot be relied on.
15. Apart from this, on perusal of IMV report marked at Ex-P21 and 22, it reveals that on that day the accident has not caused due to the any mechanical defect of the above said vehicles.
All these documents clearly shows that due to the sole rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Eicher milk lorry and in the said accident petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Under such circumstances,
the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.

Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the negligence of driver of the Eicher milk lorry bearing No.KA-02-AC-3903 and in the said accident petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
As such, I answer issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
16. ISSUE NO.2:
As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of Eicher milk truck vehicle No.KA- 02-AC-3903.
Therefore the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
17. AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME:
So far as the age of petitioner is concerned, the petitioner contended that at the time of accident he was aged 30 years.
The petitioner has produced Ex-P29-aadhaar card, Ex-P30-pan card, Ex-P31- two marks card, Ex-P32 aadhaar card, Ex-P33-pan card.
From the said documents, it reveals the date of birth of the petitioner was 29-11-1990.
So, as on the date of accident i.e., on19-2-2020 the petitioner was aged 30 years.

18. The petitioner has stated that he was working as Senior Technical Support Engineer and earning Rs.1,55,000/- per month and due to accidental injuries, he is suffering from permanent disability and deformity.

The petitioner has got examined one Asha Devi-Regional HR at VM Ware Software India private limited as PW-5 and she has produced Ex-P40-appointment letter of petitioner,
Ex-P40 to 54-salary slips, Ex-P55-60-form No.16, Ex-P61-termination record, Ex-P62-65B Evidence Act. The petitioner has produced Ex-P40 appointment letter of the petitioner which depicts that petitioner was working at V.M.Ware software India Pvt., Ltd., has offered the post of Technical support engineer to the petitioner and petitioner has accepted the said offer and was appointed as a technical support engineer on June 11, 2014.

Thus it is clear from the Ex-P40 and evidence of PW-5 it clearly reveals that petitioner was appointed as technical support engineer on 25-6-2014 and petitioner has completed his probation on 27-2-2015.

Further PW-5 has clearly deposed that Salman Shariff vs Suresh G.C on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133023177/
5 petitioner had drawn salary including all flexible components and allowances of Rs.1,51,250/-p.m.
subject to tax and other statutory deductions as on s February 2020.
In support of his contention petitioner has examined the Manager of the Axis bank as PW-6 and he has produced the bank statement of the petitioner marked at Ex-P64.
Even in the cross examination clearly stated that all employees of the V.M.Care private limited company opened their account in their Axis bank.
As per Ex-P64 the bank statement the salary of the petitioner was credited to his bank account every month.
19. Further in support of her contention, PW-5 has produced the salary slips of the petitioner marked at Ex-P41 to 54.
On perusal of which, it clearly reveals that as on February 2020 petitioner was drawing the salary of rs.1,51,250/-.
Further PW-5 has produced Ex-P55 to 60 form No.16 for the year 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021 upto 7-7- 2021.
As per Ex-P58 form No.16 for the year 2020 the petitioner has paid Rs.4,02,611.66 tax towards his annual income for the year 2019-2020.

Thus annual income of the petitioner would be Rs.1,51,250/- x 12= Rs.18,15,000/- and income tax of Rs.4,02,611/- and professional tax of Rs.200/ per month amounting to Rs.2,400/- is to be deducted from the same.
Hence income of the petitioner considered as Rs.14,09,989/- per annum and it would come to Rs.1,17,499.083 which is rounded off to Rs.1,17,500/-per month.
20. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:-

As per the Ex-P24-wound certificate of Sagar hospital, the petitioner has sustained injuries i.e., (1) head injury with diffuse axonal injury and bilateral multiple intracerebral contusions (2) bilateral proximal 1/3rd femur shaft fracture, left acetabulum fracture with left clavicle fracture (3) right knee ligamentous injury (grade 3 medial collateral ligament injury and anterior cruciate ligament avulsion injury) and doctor opined that the said injuries are grievous in nature.

Ex.P25-discharge summary of Sagar hospital discloses that petitioner took treatment as inpatient from 19-2-2020 to 3-3-2020 and in the said hospital surgery done i.e., bilateral femur IM nailing done on 19-2-2020 and ORIF posterior column acetabulum +
ORIF ilium + ORIF anterior column acetabulum left side done on 25-2-2020.

Further petitioner took treatment as inpatient at NH Narayana multispeciality hospital as inpatient from 3-3-2020 to 30-3-2020 wherein diagnosed as traumatic brain injury, multiple bone fracture and pneumonia.
21. It is the specific case of the petitioner that owing to the accidental injuries he has become disabled and has lost his earning capacity.

The petitioner has got examined one Pravin C-Senior Manager at Sagar hospital as PW-1 and got marked Ex-P1 to 5 i.e., Ex-P1-authorisation letter, Ex-P2 and 3- inpatient records, Ex-P2(a) discharge summary, Ex-P4- six CT scan film and Ex-P5-five MRI scan film.
22.

Further petitioner got examined one Lokesh B.N.-MRO- at M.H.Narayana hospital as PW-2 who has produced Ex-P6- authorisation letter, Ex-P7 and 8-inpatient records, Ex-P9- five x-rays,
Ex-P10-CD, Ex-P11 and 12-discharge summaries.
23.

Further petitioner got examined Dr.Veeresha U.Mathad- Senior consultant Neurosurgeon at Manipal hospital, Bangalore as PW-3 who has stated that petitioner was brought to him for neurological disability assessment and giving evidence on available hospital medical records,
radiological investigations and neurological disability based on the clinical examination and Salman Shariff vs Suresh G.C on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133023177/
6 neuropsychological assessment report.

Further stated that petitioner was treated as inpatient at Sagar hospital, his CT, MRI scan of had, x-rays shows following multiple injuries i.e., bilateral multiple intracerebral contusions, right gangliocapsulanic bleed, diffuse axonal injury, bilateral proximal 1/3 femur fracture, left acetabulum 3, left clavicle fracture, right knee ligament injury.

PW-3 further stated that petitioner admitted at Sagar hospital, Bangalore for treatment of severe traumatic brain injury and diagnosed having severe head injury (diffuse axonal injury) with above mentioned orthopaedic fractures and treated with conservative management for brain injury in ICU,
on ventilator support and petitioner underwent tracheostomy.

PW-3 further stated that petitioner underwent two orthopaedic surgeries on 19-2-2020 and 25-2-2020 and managed postoperatively in ICU on ventilator with analgesics, antibiotics, PPI, cerebral antioedema measure.
PW-3 further stated that at the time of discharge petitioner was unconscious, not obeying commands on ventilator, on Ryles tube for feeding.
PW-3 further stated that petitioner was readmitted to N.H.hospital, Mysore on 2-4-2020 for treatment of breathing difficulty and was managed medically and discharged on 10-4-2020.

PW-3 further stated that petitioner's present complaints are (informant is mother, brother) petitioner is bedridden, no further improvement in his condition, not able to getup, not able to roll on the bed, weakness of both hands and legs, not able to speak at all,
needs constant supervision and help of either parents for daily activities like feeding, passing urine and stool, bathing, making him roll on bed from one side to other side, needs mother support for feeding the food, does not recognise the person, does not understand no response to command or no communication with others, does not have control over the urination and passing stools.

24. PW-3 further stated that petitioner is bedridden, open eyes spontaneously, no eye contact present, his GC score is poor, E4VTM4, he does not recognise person, not obeying or following commands, does not understand anything, higher mental functions cannot be assessed as petitioner is not communicating with others, petitioner is on tracheostomy tube for breathing, foleys catheter for urination.

PW-3 further stated that petitioner underwent a detailed neuropsychological evaluation by the psychologist on 17-9- 2022, his neuropsychological disability was very difficult to assess since it was difficult to administer the test battery on him, but is is obvious that he has a severe disability.
PW-3 assessed permanent neurological disability of 88%.
PW-3 stated that petitioner has a final wholebody disability due to permanent physical impairment due to neurological conditions is 88% due to head injury which is severe disability.
Further opined that he is bedridden and dependent on others for his daily routine activities and hence has 100% functional disability irrespective of the type of avocation.

PW-3 produced Ex-P13-clinical notes, Ex-P14 &
15-Neurological and CT scan report, Ex-P16-CT scan brain report.

25. Considering the nature and gravity of injuries, line of treatment and present condition of the petitioner being bedridden, open eyes spontaneously, no eye contact present, his GC score is poor,
E4VTM4, he does not recognise person, not obeying or following commands, does not understand anything, higher mental functions cannot be assessed as petitioner is not communicating with others, petitioner is on tracheostomy tube for breathing, foleys catheter for urination.
Even looking into the photos of the petitioner produced at the time of arguments clearly shows the mental and physical condition of the petitioner.

Salman Shariff vs Suresh G.C on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133023177/
7 26.
In a ruling reported in 2023 ACJ 490 between Manjunath / Sunil and Another, the injured aged about 27 years suffered brain hemorrhage with damaged frontal and temporal lobes affecting his memory.
Tribunal in absence of evidence of doctor regarding disability suffered by the injured awarded certain sum towards medical expenses and pain and agony.

The injured was examined by a doctor pursuant to an order of appellate court who opined that insured's memory is decreasing he is unable to do any work and assessed permanent disability at 50 percent.

Appellant court taking in to consideration the notional income of the petitioner added 40 percent of income towards future prospects adopted multiplier 18, considering that injured cannot do any work assessed functional disability of 100 percent.

27. When petitioner is not in a position to get up from the bed and when since three years he is in lying condition depending upon his family members to do all his day to day work under, such circumstances the court has to consider without any second thought the physical and functional disability of the petitioner as 100%.

On appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctor,
economical or functional disability to the extent of 100%, cannot be ruled out.

Therefore, I consider the functional disability of petitioner at 100%.
28.
As per Sarla Verma's case, the appropriate multiplier applicable to the age group of 26-30 is '17'.
This Tribunal has already assessed the income of the petitioner at Rs.1,17,500/-.
Hence a sum of Rs.2,39,70,000/- (Rs.1,17,500/-X 12 X 17 X 100/100) is awarded under this head.
Hence considering the nature of injuries sustained, period of treatment taken, this court is of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads.
29. PAIN & SUFFERINGS :

As per the wound certificate the petitioner has sustained injuries i.e., (1)
head injury with diffuse axonal injury and bilateral multiple intracerebral contusion (2) bilateral proxymal 1/3rd femur shaft fracture, left acetabulum fracture, left clavicle fracture (3) right knee ligamental injury and doctor opined that the said injuries are grievous in nature.
Ex. P25 to 28-discharge summary discloses that petitioner took treatment as inpatient for 48 days on 4 occasions and underwent surgery.
The petitioner has sustained severe pain and sufferings due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident.
The petitioner has stated that he is still suffering from disability and discomforts.
Hence petitioner is suffering from with whole physical and mental pain and agony and injuries sustained by him.
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner being 30 years and certainly undergone severe pain and mental agony.
Looking into the nature of the wounds and age of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- under this head.

30. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD:
When percentage of functional disability of petitioner is taken as 100% and court proceeds to award compensation under the head loss of future income by considering the functional disability of petitioner at 100% under such circumstances the question of awarding compensation under the head loss of income during laid down period does not arise.
Salman Shariff vs Suresh G.C on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133023177/
8 31.
ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES:
From the evidence of Pw1 and as borne out by medical records, petitioner has taken treatment for several times.
Further for 48 days of hospitalization requires an attendant, was traveled to hospital for treatment.

He has taken nourishment and need further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.3,00,000/- taking in to consideration the cost of living and value of the money during the year 2020.

Even till this date,
petitioner is bedridden and under care of attendant and throughout the life time petitioner has to be looked into and taken care by the attendant.

Hence considering the above fact that an attendant is required for the petitioner throughout his life time this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.3,00,000/-
under this head.
32. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
As stated supra petitioner has suffered 100 percent disability and has suffered grievous head injuries and in vegetative condition and bed ridden, no eye contact present, GC score is poor and he does not recognize person and does not understand anything and not in a position to do any work and enjoy the life.
Even it has affect on his life expectation.
Even petitioner being age of 30 years has completely lost his marriage prospects and also marriage life and expectation of normal life.
Considering the nature of injuries and the age of the petitioner this tribunal deems fit award Rs.3 lakhs under this head.
33. MEDICAL EXPENSES:-
As regard to claim of medical expenses, the petitioner got marked the document as per Ex.P.35 i.e.,medical bills for Rs.16,26,666/-.
PW-4 in his cross examination has admitted that national insurance company has paid Rs.5 lakhs to Sagar hospital.

The petitioner has examined PW-3 who has stated that petitioner was provided with medical reimbursement facility on account of his employment with their company, he was insured with New India Assurance co., Ltd.,
valid from 15-7-2018 to 14-7- 2019, a part of the medical bills to the extent of Rs.4 lakhs only was reimbursed in part by the insurance company (directly to the hospital).
Further stated that petitioner paid Rs.1,80,504/- of medical bills.
The respondents have not disputed the said medical bills, except denial suggestion.

Upon considering the above bills and injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident, the resultant disability suffered by her due to such injuries, I proceed to award Rs.16,26,666/- under the head of medical expenses.

34. The calculation table stands as follows :
1 Pain & sufferings :
3,00,000 2 Loss of future income due : 2,39,70,000 to disability 3 Attendant charges,
:
 extra nutritious  food & conveyance 3,00,000  charges  4 Loss of future amenities & :
Salman Shariff vs Suresh G.C on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133023177/
9  happiness and marriage 3,00,000  prospectus  5 Medical expenses  16,26,666  Total  2,64,96,666

The said total amount of Rs.2,64,96,666/- is rounded off to Rs.2,64,96,700/-.
35.

During the course of argument, petitioner's counsel submitted that next friend fo petitioner has already spent more than Rs.10 lakhs towards treatment and even he is continuously spending much more amount towards day to day treatment of the petitioner and still he requires much amount for his treatment and prays to release 70 percent of the award amount and to deposit 30% of compensation amount and even filed memo to that affect.
36. REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.

37. Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the RC owner and respondent No.2 is the insurance policy holder of offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Accordingly issue No.2 is answered as 'Party in the affirmative'.
38. ISSUE NO.3:

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
-: O R D E R :-
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,64,96,700/- with interest @ 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent No.2 is hereby directed to deposit total compensation amount in this tribunal within one month from the date of this order.

Out of the compensation amount a sum equal to 30% shall be deposit in the name of petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of father of the petitioner's choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 70% shall be release to the father of the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification and verification.

However the said petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on his deposit Salman Shariff vs Suresh G.C on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133023177/
10 amount from time to time.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.

This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation of Rs.6 crores for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.
Hence prays to award compensation of Rs.6 crores from the respondents.
3. Inspite of due service of notice to the respondents, respondent No.1 remained absent and placed exparte.

4. The respondent No.2 in its written statement stated that it has issued insurance policy in favour of the 1 st respondent with respect to his vehicle No.KA-02-AC-3903 covering the risk of the said vehicle.
Further respondent No.2 contended all the petition averments as false.
Further contented that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is very exorbitant.

On the other hand, respondent seriously disputed the cause and manner and occurrence of the accident and contended that the accident had been taken place due to the sole rash and negligent driving of the petitioner himself.

When petitioner is not in a position to get up from the bed and when since three years he is in lying condition depending upon his family members to do all his day to day work under, such circumstances the court has to consider without any second thought the physical and functional disability of the petitioner as 100%.
On appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctor,
economical or functional disability to the extent of 100%, cannot be ruled out.
Therefore, I consider the functional disability of petitioner at 100%.
28.
The petitioner has stated that he is still suffering from disability and discomforts.
Hence petitioner is suffering from with whole physical and mental pain and agony and injuries sustained by him.
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner being 30 years and certainly undergone severe pain and mental agony.
Looking into the nature of the wounds and age of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- under this head.
30. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD:
When percentage of functional disability of petitioner is taken as 100% and court proceeds to award compensation under the head loss of future income by considering the functional disability of petitioner at 100% under such circumstances the question of awarding compensation under the head loss of income during laid down period does not arise.

under this head.
